At low power output, the minimum EVSE efficiency is around 80%, it peaks around 97% at 8 kW of output power, and then it settles to 90% for the remainder of the operating range. From 10 kW to the peak output power at 400 VDC, the efficiency holds steady. So, for most of the charging cycle, the EVSE operates at 90% efficiency due to loads remaining relatively high over the majority of the charging cycle, as shown later. These tests inform how much power is lost in the EVSE itself, whereas the vehicle tests below provide the power lost in both the vehicle and EVSE during a charge session. Figure 7 plots the results of a high-utilization characterization test with the Delta EVSE hardware. This test involves drawing maximum power for a period of time using a vehicle emulator and then resting for a short time; this is repeated twice afterward. This high-power pulse stresses the system, and the short rests mean the system temperatures are not allowed to come back to ambient. Figure 7. The vehicle was soaked in both cold and ambient (23°C) temperatures before testing to create a cold version of the transfer functions. Cold tests were done using the outside environment, so test time was limited to winter, and outside temperature varied. Specifications for the vehicle tests can be found in Appendix A. Hyundai and Bosch test data In this test there is a notch in the output power, which in this case represents the power going into the battery, so the delta between input and output power is wider in the early stages of the charging sequence versus the rest of the sequence. This is due to the battery heater running to bring the battery up into operating range. For this test the vehicle was soaked in cold weather overnight without preconditioning the battery before plugging it in. The minimum current test is meant to determine the minimum charge current that the EVSE can provide and the vehicle will accept. This information can then be used by the SCM system so that it knows how much it can curtail a charge before the vehicle charging session needs to be manually reinitiated.
